D=/dev/shm/$(basename {{TEMP}}); mkdir -p $D && mv src/f.txt $D/f.txt && cat $D/f.txt && stat -c %a $D/f.txt; rm -rf $D
cases.note: Cross-device (EXDEV) test: the source lives in the case temp dir (under the OS temp dir, like upstream's tmpdir()) and the destination in a unique directory on /dev/shm (tmpfs, a different device on typical Linux systems; upstream picks /dev/shm or /tmp when on a different device and skips otherwise). The script creates and removes the /dev/shm directory itself. If /dev/shm happens to be on the same device, the case still passes (same observable result via rename). The copy+unlink fallback must preserve the permission bits (0640); checked with GNU `stat -c %a`.

template: D=/dev/shm/$(basename {{TEMP}}); mkdir -p $D/d; echo precious > $D/d/f.txt; mv src/d $D || echo mv-failed; cat $D/d/f.txt src/d/f.txt; rm -rf $D
cases.note: Cross-device (EXDEV) test: the source lives in the case temp dir (under the OS temp dir, like upstream's tmpdir()) and the destination in a unique directory on /dev/shm (tmpfs, a different device on typical Linux systems; upstream picks /dev/shm or /tmp when on a different device and skips otherwise). The script creates and removes the /dev/shm directory itself. If /dev/shm happens to be on the same device, the case still passes (same observable result via rename). Upstream checks stderr contains 'not empty' and a non-zero exit code; Bun 1.4.2 prints 'mv: <dst>/d: Directory not empty' and exits 39 (ENOTEMPTY) -- the exit code is observed here via `|| echo mv-failed` because the script must clean up afterwards.

template: D=/dev/shm/$(basename {{TEMP}}); mkdir -p $D; chmod 000 src/tree; mv src/tree $D || echo mv-failed; chmod 700 src/tree; ls $D; cat src/tree/a.txt; rm -rf $D
cases.note: Cross-device (EXDEV) test: the source lives in the case temp dir (under the OS temp dir, like upstream's tmpdir()) and the destination in a unique directory on /dev/shm (tmpfs, a different device on typical Linux systems; upstream picks /dev/shm or /tmp when on a different device and skips otherwise). The script creates and removes the /dev/shm directory itself. If /dev/shm happens to be on the same device, the case still passes (same observable result via rename). Must not run as root (root bypasses the 000 permission). Upstream also asserts exitCode 13 (EACCES) for the mv; Bun 1.4.2 does exit 13, but here failure is observed via `|| echo mv-failed` because permissions must be restored (chmod 700) afterwards so the temp dir can be removed. `ls $D` printing nothing proves the destination was not created.
